Wrangell (port locode USWRG) is an Alaskan cruise port and city with population around 2,500. The town is located on Wrangell Island (Alexander Archipelago, southeastern Alaska, USA).

Wrangell Island has land area approx 544 km2 (210 mi2), ranking it the USA's 29th-largest. The island is separated from the mainland USA by Blake Channel. The island is heavily forested and has abundant wildlife. Thoms Place (the community) is on the island's southwestern coast, across Zimovia Strait from Etolin Island. Almost all of the island's territory is a federally protected nature sanctuary. 

The Indigenous Tlingit people and their ancestors inhabited Wrangell Island for thousands of years, migrating down the Stikine River when it flowed underneath the glaciers. Bear Totem Store was built during the 1920s and housed a huge collection of Indigenous arts and crafts, along with irreplaceable totem poles. A severe fire in the early 1950s burned much of downtown Wrangell and destroyed the Bear Totem Store along with most of its historic buildings.

The local economy is based on tourism, logging and fishing. Wrangell has two major forms of transportation: airplanes and ferries. Alaska Marine Highway (AMHS) includes the port on its Inside Passage route. The town is served by regularly scheduled northbound and southbound ferry crossings linking it to mainland Alaska.

During summer, the port is also visited on Mondays, Fridays and Saturdays via Inter-Island Ferry Authority's cruiseferry MV Stikine. The roundtrip starts in Prince of Wales Island's Coffman Cove, continues to Wrangell, Petersburg (Mitkof Island), and returns to Wrangell and Ketchikan (Revillagigedo Island).

Wrangell Airport receives 2 daily scheduled flights (1 morning, 1 evening) by Alaska Airlines' Boeing 737-400 aircraft. island's primary road is Zimovia Highway (running along the west coast). Most roads on the island are unpaved, forest service roads. There are also many hiking and logging trails.

Wrangell AK cruise terminal

In July 2026, American Cruise Lines/ACL announced plans to construct a floating dock in Wrangell. Currently, ACL is in negotiations for a port development plan, which requires additional investments by the city.

Reportedly, ACL will invest USD 3 million to build a floating dock on the waterfront, near the James & Elsie Nolan Center, a modern multipurpose facility at 296 Campbell Drive in the historic downtown.

The floating dock is designed to accommodate ships during overnight port calls.

Development work will involve filling two acres of the waterfront with rocks to allow for the dock's deployment. In addition to the upland site, the new dock could also be used for cargo handling and other activities.

According to ACL, the facility could be ready and operational by 2027.

Previously, local media sources suggested using the hull of American Empress (2003-built/2025-scrapped paddlewheeler) as a foundation for the new dock. The 23-year-old American Empress was dismantled in November 2025 in Wrangell, where the large boat was tied up at a former mill property. Its hull was converted into a floating deck barge by Tideline Construction.
